name: Plant structural steel design
principle: Process plants are steel frames carrying piping, equipment, platforms and loads under gravity, wind, thermal, seismic and blast demands. Designers size members and connections to structural steel codes (EN 1993, AISC 360, ISO 19902 offshore) with deflection and vibration limits that matter as much as strength: pipe rack spans, equipment nozzle flexibility and platform vibration all drive the geometry. Hot-rolled sections dominate onshore; plate girders, tubulars and cast nodes dominate offshore.

process_steps.name: Loads gathered: dead, live, piping, wind, seismic, thermal, blast
Arrangement set: bays, bracing, support locations aligned with piping and access
Members and connections designed to code with serviceability checks
Detailing, galvanising/painting, and connection design for fabrication

limitations: late piping changes propagate into steel redesign — freezing steelwork late is the classic schedule risk
thermal expansion of headers needs sliding supports and guides that survive both hot and cold cases
advantages: standardised, fabricable, demountable framing suits modular construction
steel density keeps topsides weight — the offshore design currency — under control
